Does merge_rerun drop a reviewer's finding that a DIFFERENT reviewer raised in a re-run chunk?
merge_rerun rebuilds prior findings as Finding objects that drop the reviewer, and filters prior chunk_findings with no reviewer check, so a --chunk re-run of reviewer b drops a HIGH raised by reviewer a in that chunk.
runner.merge_rerun keeps a prior finding only when its chunk is not re-run or not in this cut; the Finding dataclass carried no reviewer, so a finding did not say whose it was.

chunk_findings.detail: The fix relies on `_kept_over_rerun` reading `f.get("reviewer", "")` to distinguish a peer reviewer's prior finding, but the rerun's own findings are appended unchanged as `+ res.findings`. The new `ReviewFinding.reviewer` field defaults to `""` (`ddflow/services/review/model.py:ReviewFinding`), and no changed line stamps the current rerun reviewer onto the `ReviewFinding` objects produced by that run. Concrete failure: reviewer A records a chunk-2 HIGH in the prior panel record with `reviewer=""`; reviewer B re-runs chunk 2 and returns no findings. In `_kept_over_rerun`, `raiser` is `""`, so `bool(raiser) and raiser != who` is `False`; the HIGH is dropped and the result is a false pass. The current reviewer's identity must be set on every finding produced by the review before `merge_rerun` consumes/serializes it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/runner.py:_kept_over_rerun / merge_rerun

data.probe: Recorded chunk_findings always carry a non-empty reviewer name (_reviewed_findings: who = r.reviewer, a configured reviewer's name, never empty), so the 'reviewer=""' premise of the claimed false pass cannot occur; the regression test covers the real case (peer reviewer='a' kept over reviewer='b' re-run). The 'stamp the reviewer onto findings' gap was additionally hardened in merge_rerun+evidence().

chunk_findings.detail: Using `f.family or self.family` cannot preserve a valid empty family. A peer finding with `reviewer="a"` and `family=""` inside a record whose `self.family="acme"` is serialized as `"family":"acme"` because `""` is falsy. Since `family` defaults to `""` and empty is allowed, the fallback should key on absence, not truthiness. This corrupts the per-finding identity the change is adding, and the same `or` fallback is repeated in `ddflow/api/review/records.py:172` and `ddflow/api/review/records.py:211`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/model.py:516

chunk_findings.detail: Records persisted before the reviewer field existed still have `chunk_findings` entries with no `reviewer`. For such a finding in a re-run chunk when `_in_rerun_cut(prior, f)` is true, the function reaches `raiser = f.get("reviewer", "")` and returns `bool(raiser) and raiser != who`, which is `False`. The prior HIGH is dropped. Concretely: prior has chunk 2 with no reviewer and no other findings; reviewer `b` re-runs chunk 2 with `res.findings=[]`. `merge_rerun(prior, res)` then leaves `res.findings == []` and returns `""`, the same false-pass route the change claims to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/runner.py:_kept_over_rerun

chunk_findings.detail: The stamping loop after the merge operates on the entire merged `res.findings`, not just the re-run's own fresh findings. A pre-fix prior finding kept from a chunk outside `again` but lacking `reviewer` is silently rewritten to `res.reviewer`. Example: prior has a HIGH in chunk 1 with no reviewer; reviewer `b` re-runs only chunk 2 with no new findings. The chunk-1 finding becomes attributed to `b`. If `b` later re-runs chunk 1, `_kept_over_rerun` sees `raiser == "b"` and drops that HIGH, recreating the false-pass route.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/runner.py:merge_rerun

chunk_findings.detail: `merge_rerun` stamps every merged finding that lacks a reviewer with `res.reviewer`, not only the re-run's own findings. A panel record's other-chunk findings often have no per-finding reviewer. Given prior `chunk_findings=[{chunk:1, digest:"p", reviewer:""}]` and a chunk-2 re-run by reviewer `b` with no new findings, chunk 1 is kept by `_kept_over_rerun` and then labeled `b`. A later `--chunk 1` re-run by `b` treats that digest as its own (`raiser == who`) and drops it, which is the same false pass this change is meant to stop; a re-run by `a` keeps it forever because it now looks like `b`'s.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/runner.py:708

chunk_findings.detail: `_kept_over_rerun` drops a re-run-cut finding whenever `reviewer` is missing (`return bool(raiser) and raiser != who`), which contradicts the comment that a finding is replaced only when the same reviewer raised it. The reported probe — prior chunk-2 finding with no reviewer, `merge_rerun` by `b` with `res.findings == []` — still returns `""` and `res.findings == []`, so reviewer `a`'s HIGH is still discarded. The new test never hits that input; it only passes because the fixture already sets `"reviewer": "a"`.

chunk_findings.detail: For an old/pre-fix `ReviewResult` whose `Finding` objects still deserialize with the new default `reviewer=""` and `family=""`, the owning result still has the known `r.reviewer`/`r.family`. The previous code stamped every emitted chunk finding with those result-level values; the new `out.append({**fd})` emits the empty per-finding values as-is. Example input: a pre-fix result with `r.reviewer="b"`, `r.family="acme"`, one chunk-2 `Finding` with no per-finding reviewer. The aggregate now records that finding as `reviewer=""`, even though the real raiser is known. Downstream, `merge_rerun` can then treat it as an unattributed finding and, as the added no-reviewer test codifies, keep it after a clean re-run of reviewer `b`, leaving a stale false positive. The fallback to the known result reviewer/family should be kept for empty per-finding values; only non-empty carried reviewer attribution should be preserved verbatim.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:165

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback `if not raiser: return True` means an old unattributed finding in a re-run chunk is never replaced, even when the re-run is performed by the same reviewer. Concrete input: prior record has one chunk 2 HIGH with no `"reviewer"` field (old record), and `res` is a re-run of chunk 2 by that same reviewer with `res.findings == []`. `merge_rerun` returns the old HIGH, so the same reviewer’s own withdrawal cannot clear it; this is a false fail. The code cannot prove the finding belongs to a peer, so silently keeping it is not safe fallback.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/runner.py:_kept_over_rerun

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims the point is that “the reviewer must be able to tell a peer's finding from the one re-run,” but it only asserts `len(res.findings) == 1` and `res.findings[0].digest == "abc123"`. Given the prior chunk-2 finding with no `reviewer` and `res.reviewer == "b"`, an implementation that keeps the finding but sets its reviewer to `"b"` (for example, by stamping every kept finding with the current reviewer) still passes. The attribution half of the fix is therefore untested for legacy findings, so an incorrect implementation would be accepted.

chunk_findings.detail: The function returns `True` before checking `raiser != who` when `_in_rerun_cut(prior, f)` is false. A finding that was carried into the prior record from an earlier cut is therefore never replaced on a later re-run, even when its `reviewer` field matches the re-run reviewer. Concrete input: reviewer `a` raises HIGH on chunk 2 in the first record; reviewer `b` re-runs chunk 2, and `merge_rerun` keeps `a`'s HIGH as a peer finding, so the resulting record carries that finding. When reviewer `a` later re-runs chunk 2 with an empty result, `_in_rerun_cut(prior, a_high)` is false, so `_kept_over_rerun` returns `True` and the stale HIGH remains even though its named reviewer `a` is the re-run reviewer. The same-reviewer replacement guarantee in the docstring is defeated for any finding that has been carried over a re-run once.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/runner.py:_kept_over_rerun

chunk_findings.detail: `_kept_over_rerun` decides a finding belongs to the re-run reviewer by `reviewer` alone: `return raiser != who`. But `_stamp_raised_by` records both `reviewer` and `family` on every finding, so two distinct reviewers in different families can share the same `reviewer` value. Concretely, `prior["chunk_findings"]` contains a chunk-2 HIGH from `{"reviewer": "b", "family": "globex"}` and the re-run result has `res.reviewer == "b"`, `res.family == "acme"`, `res.findings == []`. `_kept_over_rerun` sees `raiser == who == "b"` and returns `False`, dropping the globex reviewer's HIGH as if it were the re-run reviewer's own stale finding. That is the same false-pass drop this change is meant to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/runner.py:_kept_over_rerun

chunk_findings.detail: The refutation of the earlier attribution finding does not hold for a pre-fix result that is only re-aggregated. `_stamp_raised_by` runs in `review()` and `merge_rerun`, but a panel record saved before this change deserializes `Finding` with the new default `reviewer=""` / `family=""` and is not passed through those functions again. Given that input (`r.reviewer="a"`, `r.family="acme"`, one chunk finding with no per-finding reviewer), both emitters now copy the empty fields (`out.append({**fd})` and `"reviewer": f.reviewer` / `"family": f.family`). The previous code stamped `r.reviewer` / `r.family` on every emitted finding of that result. This is not the carried-legacy case the probe describes: nothing has been merged onto another reviewer, so the owning result's identity is still the raiser, and the aggregate now records the finding as unattributed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:170

It is settled by triage or a FULL re-review where the chunk numbers correspond again. This is the safe direction (finding kept), not a false pass.
